nyciml-2005-06-fall-sophfrosh-01.prompt: Compute the number of subsets of the letters in the word "shark" that contain a "k".

nyciml-2005-06-fall-sophfrosh-02.prompt: Compute the number of zeros at the end of $126!$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-sophfrosh-03.prompt: $524a7$ is divisible by $3$. Compute the number of possible values for $a$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-sophfrosh-04.prompt: A farmer sells chickens and ducks. Chickens are \$4 each and ducks are \$7 each. At the end of the day, he has collected \$50. If $c$ represents the number of chickens sold, and $d$ the number of ducks sold, compute all possible ordered pairs $(c, d)$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-sophfrosh-05.prompt: Jack can paint a room in $8$ hours. Jill can paint the same room in $6$ hours. If Jill works alone for two hours and then Jack starts to help her, compute the number of minutes, to the nearest minute that Jack will work to complete painting of the room.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-sophfrosh-06.prompt: Rectangle $ABCD$ in the diagram consists of nine congruent rectangles. If the area of $ABCD$ is $8820$, compute the perimeter of $ABCD$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-sophfrosh-07.prompt: Compute the number of arrangements of all of the letters in the word "sharks" that begin with a "k".

nyciml-2005-06-fall-sophfrosh-08.prompt: The three digit number $3a6$ is added to $219$ and the result is divisible by $9$. Compute all possible values for $a$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-sophfrosh-09.prompt: In regular hexagon $ABCDEF$, compute the number of diagonals that do not contain either point $A$ or point $C$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-sophfrosh-10.prompt: Compute the largest $n$ for which $2^n$ is a divisor of $80!$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-sophfrosh-11.prompt: $765ab4$ is divisible by $36$. Compute all ordered pairs $(a, b)$ for which this is possible.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-sophfrosh-12.prompt: In the town of Hogsmeade, all streets are numbered consecutively from $1$ to $n$, and all avenues, which are perpendicular to the streets, are named consecutively from A to Z. If Fred is at $17^{\text{th}}$ Street and Avenue Q and wishes to go to Zonko's Joke Shop, which is on $12^{\text{th}}$ Street and Avenue K, compute the number of different paths he may take, if at no point can he be going in the opposite direction from a direction he was traveling earlier.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-sophfrosh-13.prompt: A triangle with sides of integral length has two sides that measure $6$ and $13$. Compute the number of possible lengths for the third side.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-sophfrosh-14.prompt: A rectangular solid has faces with surface areas of $9$, $12$, and $27$. Compute the volume of the solid.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-sophfrosh-15.prompt: The arithmetic mean (average) of five consecutive integers is $10$. Compute the sum of the largest and the smallest of these integers.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-sophfrosh-16.prompt: Farmer Brown raises rabbits. At first, he has only pregnant mothers in his rabbit house. Five of the mother rabbits had twins and eight of the mother rabbits had triplets, while all other mothers had one child. If the total number of rabbits in the rabbit house is now $67$, compute the number of mothers.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-sophfrosh-17.prompt: For natural numbers $a$, $b$ and $c$, when $a$ is divided by $7$ the remainder is $5$, when $b$ is divided by $7$ the remainder is $6$ and when $c$ is divided by $7$, the remainder is $1$. Compute the remainder when $a + b + c$ is divided by $7$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-sophfrosh-18.prompt: The New York City Chess Team has $89$ members, which includes the captain. The captain of the team is ill and has to call off the practice session. By arrangement, she calls four members and they each call four members, and so on, until all members have been notified. Compute the greatest number of members who will not have to make a call.
